To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the extracellular application to the intact brain of the protein kinase M inhibitor staurosporin blocks long-term potentiation in the Schaffer collaterals-CA1 and perforant path-grannle cell synapses.

the induction of long-term potentation in the Schaffer-collateral-CA1 synaptic region of the rat hippocampal slice preparation and the perforant path- granule cell synaptic region of the intact hippocampal formation is blocked by staurosporine; that this protein kinase inhibitor is membrane-permeant; that when cultured hippocampal neurons are treated with staurospirone, fluorescence is observed in both the cytoplasmic and the neuritic compartments of the cell; and
(1) staurosporine blocks the induction of long-term potentation; and (2) staurosporin has access to the cell interior and inhibits the activity of protein kinase M in the cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of long-term synaptic plasticity in the hippocampus, a structure involved in learning and memory.
the molecular mechanisms of learning and memory.
the mechanisms of synaptic plasticity in the mammalian central nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
protein kinases are not involved in the maintenance of long-term synaptic potentiation in the hippocampus.
the maintenance of long-term synaptic enhancement in hippocampal neurons is not mediated by any protein kinase that is sensitive to inhibition by staurosporine.

the maintenance of long-term synaptic enhancement in the Schaffer collaterals-CA1 system and the induction of long-term synaptic potentiation in the perforant pathway-dentate system of the hippocampus is not mediated by a protein kinase that has access to the cell cytoplasm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
protein kinase M is involved in LTP induction, but not maintenance.
protein kinase inhibitors can be used to study the role of protein kinases in synaptic plasticity.
protein kinase M and other protein kinases do not maintain long-term synaptic potentiation in the rat hippocampus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maintenance of LTF does not require protein phosphorylation.
LTP can be maintained in the absence of protein kinase activity.
the maintenance of LPT is not mediated by constitutively active enzymes.
